messages:
maria: Observed a burst on prod where microbatches shrank and we got ~20% more soft-429s. Root cause looks like KV cache eviction spikes when a large prefix set comes in. Repro steps and perf logs attached.
ryan: thx — can you paste the sample log lines? did kernel switch happen around same time?
maria: logs: ```[2026-03-16T12:01:23Z] batch_id=xyz kernel_hint=wavkernel->matmul tokens=1200 kv_evictions=240 queue_len=18 soft_429=1``` small set of requests caused eviction storm.
sam: hmm. might be batch formation greediness—when kv miss rate jumps, effective token budget per batch changes and kernel selection flips to an expensive path -> longer tail -> admission not tightening fast enough.
devon: proposal: add a short-timescale 'eviction-aware token cap' that reduces max batch tokens when eviction rate > threshold for N secs. Also force kernel hint stickiness for existing cohorts for M secs to avoid oscillation.
ryan: +1. We should also adjust admission to prefer rejecting new requests from heavy-token lanes first (fairness lanes) instead of global shed. That keeps small requests flowing.
maria: ran a sim with a patched admit: `eviction_cap_fraction=0.6`, `stickiness_ms=4000`, per-lane weight bias=0.2 — reduced soft-429 by ~65% in replay but tail latency slightly up for heavy lanes.
sam: tradeoff seems good. Need canary in one region. Also add metric: `kv_eviction_rate` and expose in console dashboards + a golden prompt set to detect quality regressions.
devon: we should add a short circuit: if kernel switch detected more than 3 times in 30s for a worker, mark it 'no-switch' for 10s and let admission drop instead.
ryan: ops note: ensure Dedicated pools have different defaults — lower stickiness for Dedicated since capacity is stable.
maria: created a PR: https://git.redwood/evict-backoff (WIP) includes tests + perf benchmark. Can reviewers PTAL? cc @sam @ryan :thumbsup: 
infra-bot: deploy-canary started: canary-evict-backoff -> us-west-2 pool, 3 workers
sam: quick QA checklist: small synthetic with hot-prefix, replay production traces, measure `soft_429_rate`, `p50/p99`, KV hit rate.
devon: also add unit test for kernel-hint persistence across batch merges.
ryan: timeline? canary for 24h then roll to 10% if metrics stable.
maria: agreed. I'll watch dashboards and bump if regressions. Thanks :pray:
